questions.q: Why can a feature show strong average importance yet still be a poor signal to trade on?
options: Average importance scores are always computed incorrectly
Importance is usually measured once over the full sample, which can hide a signal that only worked during part of that history
Permutation importance cannot be computed on financial data
Feature importance scores are always zero for financial features
questions.explain: A signal that was strongly predictive for part of the sample and useless or harmful for the rest can still average out to a healthy-looking importance score, hiding the instability.

questions.q: What does rolling/windowed feature-importance analysis do differently from a standard importance check?
options: It only uses the first 10% of the dataset
It recomputes importance repeatedly across sliding time windows instead of once over the full sample
It ignores the target variable entirely
It replaces permutation importance with MDI
questions.explain: Rolling analysis recomputes importance (e.g., via permutation_importance) inside each of a series of sliding windows, turning one summary number into a time series that reveals stability or instability.

questions.q: What does the Information Coefficient (IC) measure?
options: The total number of features in a model
The rank correlation between a signal's predicted values and actual forward returns, typically per period
The R-squared of a linear regression on the full dataset
The number of trees in a random forest
questions.explain: IC is typically a Spearman rank correlation between predictions and actual forward returns, computed period by period to track a signal's real-world predictive power over time.

options: The information coefficient fading, reversing, or holding steady as you track it across time
A bug that causes IC calculations to always return zero
The process of removing low-importance features from a model
A method for speeding up SHAP computation
questions.explain: IC decay describes watching a signal's IC series over time or across forecast horizons to see whether the predictive edge holds up, fades, or collapses.

questions.q: Why is an unstable signal a red flag even when the overall backtest Sharpe ratio looks attractive?
options: Sharpe ratio is an average, which can hide a signal that only performed well during one regime and was flat or negative otherwise
Sharpe ratio only applies to bonds, not equities
Unstable signals always have negative Sharpe ratios by definition
Backtests cannot compute Sharpe ratios for unstable signals
questions.explain: A headline Sharpe ratio is an average across the whole backtest period, which can mask regime-dependent behavior that rolling importance or IC analysis would reveal.
